title: Pilot sync - integration edge cases & function-calling validation
topics: next steps: benchmarks and regression tests
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on integration edge cases uncovered during pilot - primarily around function-calling schema mismatches, streaming partial responses breaking JSON parsers in the app, and SDK glue code for retries and idempotency. Redwood SE to produce repro harness and run a 1k query streaming test; customer will provide two failing traces and add structured test cases to their E2E suite.
next_steps: Redwood SE to run 1k-query streaming benchmark and share results (throughput, error count, token cost) - due 2025-11-25
Customer to upload two failing traces and the app-side parser code snippet to shared drive - due 2025-11-21
Alex to send updated pilot pricing addon for extended streaming testing
Schedule 30-min SE deep dive on JSON schema validation and partial-stream handling next week
action_items: Priya Desai: create a minimal repro harness (node/python) that demonstrates function-calling truncation + streaming partials - due 2025-11-22
Samir Patel: provide two postmortem traces and the app JSON parser logs - due 2025-11-21
Carlos Nguyen: open a pilot ticket with infra team to enable higher burst for next benchmark window - due 2025-11-24
Maya Chen: add structured output validation cases to Nimbus CI targeting the fields 'invoice_items' and 'total_amount' - due 2025-11-26
transcript:
00:00 Alex: alright, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving time, this is the weekly sync for the Nimbus pilot. we want to focus today on the integration edge cases you reported, especially the function-calling and structured output issues. priya and carlos are on from our side.
00:12 Samir: thanks Alex, yeah we hit two flakes in staging yesterday; one where the function-calling response came back missing 'total_amount' and another when the streaming response arrived in two partials and our parser threw an exception.
00:25 Priya: right, we dug in last night — first note, we saw the model return the function call with the expected name but the JSON payload was trimmed mid-array, so the app deserializer choked. looks like streaming chunks sometimes split tokens inside numbers/strings which isn't ideal for naive parsers.
00:41 Jordan: just to be clear, we're using the JS SDK and our parser assumes a single complete JSON blob from the assistant response; with streaming we append chunks until we see closing brace then parse. that heuristic fails when a chunk boundary splits a multibyte char or leaves the array partially closed, so the io lib throws.
00:58 Carlos: ok, that's fairly common — streaming is intended to be incremental. for function calling we usually recommend emitting structured output using the SDK's function_call helper that guarantees each event is an atomic function call structure. can you paste the log of the raw deltas?
01:15 Samir: i uploaded two traces to the shared drive, filenames are "trace-2025-11-17-failure1.log" and "trace-2025-11-17-failure2.log". they include the raw delta payloads and our parser stack traces.
01:29 Priya: perfect, we'll grab those. quick qual question — are you using prefix caching or batching at the request layer for these endpoints?
01:37 Maya: yes, we turned on batching for throughput; prefix caching is off for this route.
01:42 Priya: batching can change chunk timing; if you're batching many short prompts, the runtime may coalesce tokens differently which can increase likelihood of mid-boundary slices. for function calling specifically we also have a 'emitOnComplete' flag in the SDK that delays the function payload until the full function body is assembled, that can be enabled as a quick workaround.
02:00 Ibrahim: from security, our concern is twofold: first, we want guaranteed schema presence for billing fields (total_amount, currency), and second, auditability — we need full function_call logs retained for 90 days in a tamper-evident way. can redwood confirm retention and tamper logs?
02:20 Alex: yes, for the pilot we're on the standard retention but we can enable longer retention; for enterprise Private/Dedicated we have configurable retention and KMS options. i'll follow up with the security packet link.
02:33 Priya: notes on schema — the best practice we've seen is to use a strict JSON schema on the client and also leverage the sdk function-calling wrapper which will surface a single structured event (no partials) if you set emitOnComplete. downside is a tiny latency bump.
02:49 Jordan: how small is tiny? in our SLA we target 250ms p95. the bump might push it over depending on load.
02:58 Carlos: fair. emitOnComplete will add a few dozen ms in normal runs; absolute delta depends on model and sequence length. you can mitigate at the routing layer — pin light models or dedicated capacity for high-SLA routes.
03:12 Samir: another problem we saw: when an early reconnect happened (client websocket flapped), some chunks were delivered twice and our idempotency keys aren't at the right granularity, so duplicate function invocations produced double charges.
03:27 Priya: yeah duplicate chunks + function execution is tricky. recommended pattern: keep function calls idempotent by including a request_id in the function args from the client. the runtime will surface the same function payload but you should dedupe on the downstream function executor side. we'll include sample code.
03:40 Maya: also the structured output sometimes had the invoice_items as a flat string rather than an array — e.g., "items: \"widget x3 - $12\"" vs [ {name:..., qty:...} ]. is that a prompt tuning issue or model hallucination?
03:56 Priya: that looks like a prompt framing problem — when the model has ambiguous instructions it can collapse arrays into conversational text. we can harden with a response schema in the prompt and a JSON schema post-validator. we ran a small rerun on 200 examples and adding the schema reduced such errors from ~8% to ~1.5%.
04:16 Samir: good to know. for billing we only accept structured invoice_items arrays. can the SDK validate and reject responses before they hit our parser?
04:26 Carlos: yes, the SDK can run a lightweight validator callback that checks required fields and shapes. if it fails you get a structured error you can handle (retry, ask clarifying prompt, fallback).
04:36 Jordan: might be useful to have the SDK expose both the raw stream and a post-assembled JSON so our older code can opt-in gradually.
04:45 Priya: absolutely, current node/python SDKs have stream events plus a convenience assembly hook. we'll share the code snippet after this call.
04:53 Ibrahim: on retention and audit logs — what format are the logs in? are they tamper-evident? do they include request/response hashes we can integrate into our SIEM?
05:04 Alex: our audit logs include timestamps, request ids, model version, route, and a content-hash. for enterprise we offer KMS-wrapped signatures for tamper-evidence. again i'll drop the security packet.
05:17 Samir: ok returning to repros: the two traces we uploaded show slightly different manifestations — one is truncated function JSON, the other is a complete function body but the inner array items were converted to a string. any chance these are separate bugs?
05:30 Priya: yes they're likely orthogonal — truncation is streaming/chunk boundary handling; array-to-string is prompt/decoder behavior. we should treat them separately and create two reproducible tests.
05:43 Maya: prioritize truncation as it's causing crashes. array coercion is bad but recoverable with validators.
05:50 Carlos: plan: priya will build a repro that simulates streaming with forced chunk boundaries and websocket reconnects, then we'll run it against your staging route with increased burst capacity. that should show whether the runtime is splitting within multibyte tokens or if the SDK assembler is at fault.
06:08 Priya: yes, i'll create both node and python harnesses. also we'll include a mode that toggles emitOnComplete so you can see tradeoffs.
06:17 Jordan: on one failing run we saw model variant fallback kick in mid-stream (we had configured smart routing). could that produce inconsistent structure?
06:27 Carlos: yes if a fallback model has different tokenizer/serialization quirks it can change chunk boundaries; we recommend pinning the model for critical routes or ensuring compatibility with the fallback. smart routing should prefer compatible variants but not all variants are identical.
06:40 Samir: is there a way to force full-deterministic outputs for billing fields? like a recommended small decode setting or temperature 0?
06:48 Priya: set temperature 0 plus nucleus sampling off and provide exact schema constraints. that reduces diversity but can reduce hallucinations. it's not 100% deterministic but helps a lot. for absolute determinism you'd need a deterministic model and identical runtime kernels; that's more of an enterprise Dedicated conversation.
07:05 Maya: ok, for the pilot we'll try temperature 0 + emitOnComplete for billing routes, and leave high-latency non-billing flows with default streaming.
07:15 Samir: anything on cost? emitOnComplete and extra validation add work — will that change our token estimates?
07:23 Alex: not significantly token-wise — emitOnComplete is a client-side assembly behavior; compute overhead is mostly negligible. model token output isn't changing. however running more retries or fallback models can increase tokens. we'll note the expected token delta in the benchmark report.
07:37 Priya: one more gotcha — if your CI uses JSON.parse on partial chunks in unit tests it may mask production streaming problems. please add end-to-end tests that exercise the real streaming protocol.
07:48 Maya: noted. we'll add streaming tests.
07:52 Carlos: next steps recap: priya builds repro harness (node/python); run 1k streaming job with emitOnComplete on/off; collect error counts, p95/p99 latency; we will share a short log of recommended sdk settings and a sample validator.
08:09 Alex: i'll send the security packet and the pilot pricing addon. samir/maya you'll drop the two traces and add the parser snippet. then we'll reconvene after the benchmark.
08:23 Samir: thanks folks — quick question: do you have a short snippet showing idempotency keys in function args? that's something we want immediately.
08:32 Priya: yes i'll paste both node and python snippets into the shared doc after call, including request_id patterns and an example dedupe table.
08:41 Jordan: small nit — sometimes the transcripts that your side provided had incorrect product names, e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' came through as 'Redwood Dedication' in the auto notes. nothing blocking but word of caution for our compliance docs.
08:59 Alex: haha, thanks for flag — automated captions do weird stuff. we'll be careful.
09:05 Maya: ok nothing else, thanks all, good progress.
09:09 Ibrahim: thanks, appreciate the security clarifications.
09:12 Alex: end recap — priya, carlos, samir are owners on repro/action; next sync invite by Alex once benchmark is ready. thanks everyone.
